description: THE GAP-PRIORITIZATION (SCHEDULING) DECISION as DATA. The jabberwock already DRIVES its fixes on BOTH dimensions -- efficiency (performance_self_improvement) and understanding (understanding_self_improvement): perceive a gap -> diagnose its shape (graph) -> select the fix (graph) -> verify (#2) -> apply. But when MULTIPLE gaps are perceived at once it did not yet DECIDE which to fix FIRST. This seed adds the SCHEDULING layer: given the perceived gaps, each carrying a MEASURED salience (efficiency: the latency-excess cold_ms - warm; understanding: the defect-severity), ORDER them most-salient-first and fix in that order -- and the ORDER comes OUT of the graph, not hardcoded Python. PRINCIPLE: salience = residual = surprise ('explore the under-compressed'); the biggest measured residual is fixed first. Cross-domain the raw magnitudes are not comparable (ms vs a 0..1 severity), so they are normalized per the agent's POLICY -- SaliencePolicyWeight nodes carrying a per-kind weight (graph data, tunable) -- stated honestly as a POLICY, NOT a false-universal metric. Two graph-resident Programs, the twins of perf_diagnose / route_pick: (1) salience_normalize reads a gap's raw salience + kind and multiplies by the policy weight for that kind (Times over an Argmin-picked SaliencePolicyWeight whose kind Eq the gap's kind -- the SAME Filter/Argmin/Attr shape perf_fix_pick uses); (2) gap_priority is an Argmax over the still-unordered agenda gaps (Filter CapabilityGap where in_agenda==1 And Not ordered==1) by their normalized salience, returning the MOST-salient one. Applied REPEATEDLY (Python marks the picked gap ordered and re-evaluates) the Program EMITS the whole order -- most-salient-first. The ORDER is the Program's output over the salience DATA: BOOST an understanding gap's salience above the efficiency gap's and the SAME Program yields a DIFFERENT order (that gap now first). Python only sequences the enactment; it never sorts the gaps.

microtheory.name: gap_prioritization
microtheory.description: the order in which perceived capability gaps are fixed: most-salient (biggest normalized measured residual) first. Salience is measured at the boundary; the normalization weights are a stated POLICY (graph data); the ORDER is the gap_priority Argmax Program's output, applied repeatedly.

attrs.name: default_salience_policy
attrs.description: cross-domain salience normalization: a per-kind weight brings the raw measured residuals (efficiency latency-excess in ms; understanding defect-severity in 0..1) onto a comparable scale. A POLICY, tunable by editing the SaliencePolicyWeight weights -- NOT a universal metric.
attrs.rationale: efficiency salience is a latency-excess in MILLISECONDS (a cold one-time init is ~1400 ms -> huge); understanding salience is a 0..1 defect-severity. Un-normalized, ms always dwarfs severity for reasons of UNIT not IMPORTANCE. The per-kind weight is the agent's stated stance on how many ms of latency-excess trade for one unit of understanding-defect.

scale a latency-excess measured in ms down by 1/1000 so 1400 ms of one-time-init excess reads as ~1.4 normalized salience -- comparable to a ~1.0 understanding defect, and still (correctly) the most salient of the three.
an understanding defect-severity is already a 0..1 residual (1 - min error-feature); keep it as-is (weight 1.0).
